name: Lorde
notes: Minimal-percussion art-pop with modal harmony. This is one of only a handful of models in the section that keeps the parent genre's half-time class, and it does so on the research's own words: "backbeat is half-time-feeling — the snare/clap lands on 3 of a slow 4/4 as often as on 2&4 — at an Andante 85 BPM on the breakout single", so `halfTime` is true and the placement is `halftime_3`. The documented 50/50 between 3 and 2&4 cannot be said in one `placement` field; it is recorded here instead of being averaged into a wrong number. Because the placement matches the parent, the separation is carried by the drum palette, which the entry gives in full: "finger snaps, a single deep kick and a hip-hop-derived backbeat — deliberately lo-fi, with long gaps and no hat bed. Percussion is a structural event, not a groove; whole verses run on snaps alone." That is `hihat.continuous` false at `fillDensity` 0.04 with the roll vocabulary off, a kick density of 1—2, a `snap`-only snare stack and a `snap`-led perc lane list at high density with a positive gain offset. Mode is the strongest harmonic fact in the entry — "Mixolydian is her documented signature mode (the breakout single is written G major functioning as D Mixolydian), i.e. major with a flattened 7th" — so `scales` is mixolydian-dominant and the flat-7 chord is in every family; "2-bar loops built from three chords" is `maxChords` 3 with a 2-bar harmonic rhythm. Melody register is the documented contralto span F♯3—F♯5 "written low and smoky", and "narrow, syllabic and back-phrased" is the step share and the low `octaveJumpProb`. The counter is not an instrument: "harmony is delivered by stacked multitracked vocals rather than instruments", so it runs at a high density as a pad. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum probability, the humanize numbers, the perc gain and `session.keys` beyond G and D — the research documents a palette and a philosophy, not a pattern, and its key line gives only "the breakout single is written G major functioning as D Mixolydian", so A and C are inferred neighbours and are not in the research. ⛔ **The bass was authored `reese_sustain` and the research does not say the bass is held.** It says *"sub-bass and synth bass on roots, mixed loud and round; the low end plus the vocal stack is often the entire arrangement"* — a level and timbre claim, not a duration one — over *"finger snaps, a single deep kick and a hip-hop-derived backbeat"*. `mirror_kick` follows that kick; `reese_sustain` emits one note per chord (TASK-162) and left this model at **287 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds** against a floor of 500. The `b7` in `cellShapes` is the sourced half — *"**Mixolydian** is her documented signature mode ... i.e. major with a flattened 7th"*. ⚠ **INFERRED:** `followRootsProb` 0.90 and `anticipationProb` 0.20 are lane-conventional rates, not sourced ones. ⛔ **`cellShapes` came out (2026-08-17, bassline variety floor), and the sourced `b7` did not go with it.** The list led with `["1"]`, a one-degree cell of the root that says exactly what `followRootsProb` already says; and because `bass.rs` prefers a cell over `passingTones`, drawing it made both `followRootsProb` and this model's own `P5`/`m7` unreadable — every note the root. Measured: **939 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds**, a 0.939 share against `bass.rs`'s 0.95. The flat-7 the Mixolydian line asks for is already authored where the engine reads it with no cell present — `passingTones: ["P5", "m7"]` — so the colour is unchanged and now lands on any note that leaves the root instead of on every other one. The research asks for no figure beyond that: *"sub-bass and synth bass on roots, mixed loud and round"*. Rhythm, register, root lock and anticipation are untouched.
